item.title: How to Use OpenCode on Windows for FREE (Install + First Project)
item.description:
Most OpenCode install guides for Windows still tell you to run npm install -g opencode-ai. Run that today and you get version 1.19. The current OpenCode is version 2, and it ships under a different npm package: @opencode/cli.

This guide installs the right version on Windows 11, connects a free AI model without paying anything, and builds a small working app from one prompt. You don’t need a GPU, because the model runs in the cloud.

This is part 1 of my OpenCode series. Everything later in the series builds on this setup.

🎥 Watch the Video

👉 Watch on YouTube: How to Use OpenCode on Windows for FREE

🧠 What Is OpenCode?

OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that runs in your terminal. You describe what you want in plain English. It reads your project, writes files and runs commands. It’s an open-source alternative to Claude Code, and you pick the model: a free one, a paid one with your own API key, or a local model through Ollama.

🧰 What You Need

  • Windows 10 or 11
  • Node.js (OpenCode installs with npm)
  • A terminal. I use Windows Terminal with PowerShell.

OpenCode runs natively on Windows, but the official docs recommend WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) for the best experience. For a beginner, native Windows is the simplest way to start, so that’s what this guide uses.

1️⃣ Step 1: Check Node.js

Open PowerShell and run:

1
2

node -v
npm -v

If both print a version number, you’re ready. If not, download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, install it with the defaults, then close and reopen your terminal. An old terminal window won’t see the new install.

2️⃣ Step 2: Install OpenCode V2 (the Right Package)

This is where most tutorials go wrong. If you installed OpenCode before, remove the old V1 package first, then install V2:

1
2
3

npm uninstall -g opencode-ai     # only if you installed V1 before
npm install -g @opencode/cli
opencode --version               # should start with 2

If the version starts with 1, the old package is still on your machine. Uninstall it and run the install again.

Two more things:

  • The V2 docs say Windows package managers (Scoop, Chocolatey, winget) aren’t supported. Use npm.
  • If you prefer a normal app window, there’s a Windows desktop app on the OpenCode download page. This guide uses the terminal version.

3️⃣ Step 3: Open a Project

OpenCode works on whatever folder you start it in. Create a new one and launch it:

1
2
3

mkdir expense-tracker
cd expense-tracker
opencode

The prompt box at the bottom of the OpenCode screen is where you type.

4️⃣ Step 4: Connect a Free Model 

1
2

/connect   -> OpenCode -> sign in
/models    -> pick a free model

Type /connect, choose OpenCode and sign in with your OpenCode account. Then type /models and pick one of the free models. OpenCode’s docs list several models as free for a limited time, including Big Pickle and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free.

Two honest notes:

  • The free list changes, so check /models for what’s free today.
  • Some free models may keep your prompts to improve the model. Don’t paste client code, passwords or API keys into a free model. For practice projects, it’s fine.

If you already have an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, /connect is also where you add it.

5️⃣ Step 5: Plan vs Build

OpenCode has two main agents, and beginners often miss this:

Agent What it does
Build (default) Writes code, edits files and runs commands
Plan Explores your project and writes a plan. It doesn’t edit your project files.

Press Shift + Tab to switch between them. My rule: start every new task in Plan, read the plan, then switch to Build. It costs one extra step and saves a lot of undoing.

🚀 Your First Project: An Expense Tracker From One Prompt

In Plan mode, paste this prompt:

1
2
3
4

Plan a simple expense tracker web app using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
I want to add an expense with an amount in rupees, a category and a date,
see the monthly total, and save everything in the browser's localStorage.
Keep it in three files.

Read the plan. If it looks right, press Shift + Tab to switch to Build and type: Go ahead and build it.

When it finishes, open index.html in your browser. Add an expense and check that the total updates. Then refresh the page: if the data is still there, localStorage is working. The video shows the full run.

⌨️ Shortcuts Worth Learning on Day One

Shortcut What it does
@ + file name Attaches a file to your prompt, e.g. @style.css add a dark mode
/undo Reverts your last message and the changes that came with it
/redo Brings an undone change back
! + command Runs a terminal command without leaving OpenCode, e.g. !dir
Esc Stops the agent mid-task
Ctrl + P Opens the command menu

⚠️ Honest Limits

  • Free models change and have limits. If one stops working or slows down, open /models and pick another.
  • Native Windows vs WSL. Native works, but the official recommendation is WSL for better file performance and terminal support. If you hit odd terminal problems, WSL is the fix.
  • Build runs commands without asking by default. OpenCode’s permission rules allow everything unless you add rules. If you want it to ask before every shell command, add an ask rule for shell (see Permissions). Either way, use Git or a test folder until you trust it.

🛠️ Quick Fixes

Problem Fix
opencode is not recognized Reopen the terminal. Still failing? Run npm config get prefix and add that folder to your PATH.
“Running scripts is disabled on this system” Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
Version shows 1.x npm uninstall -g opencode-ai, then npm install -g @opencode/cli
No free models in /models Run /connect, choose OpenCode and sign in first

❓ FAQ

Is OpenCode free? OpenCode itself is open source and free. The models are separate: OpenCode offers some free models for a limited time, and paid models need your own API key or credits.

Do I need a GPU? Not for this setup. The free models run in the cloud. You only need a GPU if you run a local model, which is the next video.

Why does opencode --version show 1.x? You installed the old opencode-ai package. Uninstall it and install @opencode/cli.

Should I use WSL instead? The official docs recommend WSL for the best experience. Native Windows is simpler for a first setup, and you can switch later.

⏭️ Next in the Series

Next up: OpenCode + Ollama. You’ll run a model on your own PC, so you don’t need an account or an internet connection for the model. Subscribe to The Code Street so you don’t miss it.

item.title: How to Connect vidIQ to Claude (Free Plan, Step-by-Step Setup)
item.description:
A channel with just 1,200 subscribers got 231K views on one GTA 6 video, and Claude found it for me in a single chat using real YouTube data from vidIQ. I did the whole thing on a brand-new free Claude account and a brand-new free vidIQ account.

This post covers how to connect vidIQ to Claude step by step, what you can do with it, and what you get on the free plans compared with paid ones.

🎥 Watch the Video

👉 Watch on YouTube: How to Connect vidIQ to Claude

🧠 vidIQ, Claude and Connectors in 30 Seconds

  • vidIQ is a YouTube research tool. It shows how many people search a topic, how crowded that topic is, which small channels are getting unusually big views (outliers), and how your own channel is doing.
  • Claude is an AI assistant by Anthropic. It’s good at ideas, scripts, titles and planning, but on its own it has no live YouTube numbers.
  • A connector links Claude to another app. You ask in plain English, Claude uses vidIQ’s tools through the connector, and real data comes back into your chat. You sign in once, and Claude asks before it uses each tool.

⚖️ Why Connect Them?

I asked the same question both ways: “Give me 5 GTA 6 video ideas that could get views fast.” Without vidIQ, the ideas sounded reasonable but had no search volume, no competition score and no proof. With vidIQ, every idea came with numbers.

🔌 How to Connect vidIQ to Claude (Free Plan)

It takes about two minutes, and you don’t need an API key or any code.

  1. Open vidIQ in Claude’s directory. In Claude, go to Plugins (the connector directory) and search for vidIQ. You can also start from vidIQ’s Claude page.
  2. Click Connect.
  3. Sign in to vidIQ. A free vidIQ account is enough. I signed up with Google.
  4. Allow access. You’ll see “Connected to Claude”, and you’re done.

Tip for free Claude users: the free plan allows only one custom connector, so add vidIQ from the directory listing as shown here. If you’d rather add it as a custom connector, the server URL is https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp.

💬 Turn It On in a Chat

  • In any chat, click + → Connectors and make sure vidIQ is on.
  • Start your prompt with “Use vidIQ to…” so Claude knows to use real data.
  • Not sure what to ask? vidIQ’s Claude page has a free prompt library you can copy from.

The first time Claude uses a vidIQ tool, it asks for permission. You can allow it once or always (more on this below).

📊 What I Did With It

1. A real channel check

I pasted this prompt from vidIQ’s library:

1

Use vidIQ to review my channel's last 90 days. Compare views, watch time, and traffic sources with the previous 90 days, then suggest three things to investigate.

On my small gaming channel, engaged views were down 35% and watch time down 18%. Average view duration went up 26%, but traffic from YouTube search dropped 41%. Claude also noticed that YouTube changed how it counts views in late August, so it compared engaged views instead of raw views. My takeaway was that my titles don’t match what people search for.

2. Video ideas with proof

Then I asked for GTA 6 video ideas. Claude ran vidIQ’s outlier search (small channels with big views) and rising keyword research (what people are searching this week), then gave ideas backed by numbers:

  • “GTA 6 funny moments”: about 945K estimated monthly searches, and a 1.2K-subscriber channel got 26.5K views on a crash compilation in two days.
  • “GTA 6 ending”: the biggest demand (about 2.7M) but also the most crowded topic.
  • GTA intro-evolution video: 231K views in four days from a channel with about 1.2K subscribers.
  • “GTA 6 4K gameplay”: about 230K searches, 38% of them from India.

These are vidIQ estimates. Treat them as a direction, not a promise. Claude also caught one search that came back in Hindi and re-ran it in English.

3. Title scoring

Finally, I asked vidIQ to score title options before choosing one. My best title scored 98 out of 100.

1

Use vidIQ to score these 4 titles and tell me which is best and why: …

💸 Do You Need to Pay?

Everything above ran on free plans.

vidIQ: Free vs Boost vs MAX

Plan Price (India, monthly) AI credits per month
Free ₹0 150
Boost ₹999 2,000
MAX ₹2,490 6,000

These were the prices on the day I recorded, and yearly billing is cheaper. Check your own price at checkout.

Most research calls cost about 5 credits each, so the free 150 credits come to roughly 30 lookups a month. That’s enough to plan a few videos. Unused credits don’t roll over.

Claude: Free vs Pro

Free Claude handled everything in this guide. You’ll sometimes see “Claude is busy, retrying” and get upgrade prompts. Pro (about ₹2,000 a month in India) adds higher usage limits, more Claude models and Claude Code.

🛡️ Permissions: Stay in Control

Go to Plugins → vidIQ → Permissions to choose which tools run automatically and which need your approval.

  • Always allow: research tools like keywords, outliers and analytics, which only read data.
  • Needs approval: anything that can change your YouTube videos, such as titles, thumbnails or video details.

✅ My Advice for New Channels

  1. Start with free Claude and free vidIQ.
  2. Find outliers from small channels in your niche.
  3. Pick searches that are rising but not crowded.
  4. Upgrade only when you post every week and keep running out of credits.

❓ FAQ

How do I connect vidIQ to Claude?

In Claude, open Plugins, find vidIQ, click Connect, sign in to vidIQ and allow access. Then turn vidIQ on from + → Connectors in a chat and start your prompt with “Use vidIQ to…”.

Can I use vidIQ in Claude for free?

Yes. The vidIQ connector works on the free vidIQ plan (150 AI credits a month) and on a free Claude account. Everything in this guide was done on free plans.

How many credits does vidIQ use in Claude?

Most research calls, such as keyword research, outliers and title scores, cost about 5 credits each. The free plan’s 150 credits come to roughly 30 lookups a month.

Do I need an API key to connect vidIQ to Claude?

No. With the directory listing you just click Connect and sign in. If you add it as a custom connector instead, the server URL is https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp.

Is it safe to give Claude access to my YouTube channel?

You stay in control. Claude asks before using each tool, and in Plugins → vidIQ → Permissions you can keep anything that changes your videos on “Needs approval” while letting read-only research tools run automatically.

Takeaways

  • Connecting vidIQ to Claude takes about two minutes, works on free plans, and needs no API key.
  • The real value is proof: every idea comes with search demand, competition and small-channel examples.
  • Start free, and upgrade only when you’re posting weekly and running out of credits.

Want free AI agents running on your own PC? Start with my Hermes Agent + Ollama setup on Windows.
